shorts.title: What you will learn: Vector operations
shorts.hook: Insert, erase, sort and find in a few lines.
shorts.script: Insert, erase, sort and find in a few lines. Today we use the vector toolbox. You will insert, erase, sort and search with only a few lines. A vector has many tools. Insert adds an item at a position. Erase removes an item at a position. Both use an iterator. The begin function gives an iterator to the first item. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: Vector operations.

shorts.title: Vector operations in one minute
shorts.script: A vector has many tools. Insert adds an item at a position. Erase removes an item at a position. Both use an iterator. The begin function gives an iterator to the first item. The algorithm header adds sort and find. Think of a train. You can add a coach in the middle, take one out, or put them in order. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Vector operations in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.hook: Sort takes the start and the end of the vector.
shorts.script: Sort takes the start and the end of the vector. It puts the items in order. The loop prints ten, twenty, thirty, forty. Find looks for thirty. It returns an iterator to the item. Subtracting begin gives the index. Thirty is at index two. The program prints the sorted numbers, and then the index two. Insert and erase need an iterator. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: Erase with a number
shorts.hook: Can you spot the bug in vector operations?
shorts.script: Can you spot the bug in vector operations? Bug of the Day. We call erase with the plain number one. The compiler says no matching function for call to erase. Erase wants an iterator, not an index. Write begin plus one, and the call works. Erase wants a position in the form of an iterator, not an index. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: Erase with a number.

Sort it, and print the smallest and the biggest. Write your answer in the comments. Insert and erase need an iterator. Begin gives an iterator to the first item. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
